title: NAME GENERATOR, SUGGEST NAME
body:
Immerse yourself in Middle-earth lore with MUME's robust
name generator, a must-have tool accessible at no cost to all
players during character
creation. Craft authentic character identities
effortlessly with tailored name suggestions inspired by J.R.R.
Tolkien's legendary universe. This
feature is also accessible in-game via the
suggest command:

Syntax:

  suggest name <gender> <race>


This command taps into MUME's name generator to propose a
name based on the specified gender and race.

Example:

  > suggest name male hobbit



  Accepted races/subraces

The name generator supports the following diverse races and
subraces:




      Beorning


      Númenórean


      Dunadan


      Dwarf




      Eriadorian


      Half-elf


      Hobbit


      Noldor




      Orc


      Rohir


      Troll


      Silvan




      Sindar








  Some notes



    Orc and troll
    characters, regardless of gender,
    draw from the same name pool.


    Beornings and Eriadorians share a name pool.


    Oldelf and oldorc were works in progress which both have decent-sized name
    pools to draw from. Their eventual fate is undecided.


    Half-elves utilize the Sindarin name pool.



  Words of warning

The name generator yields millions of potential names, some
of which may not be suitable. Expect a mix of good and bad
suggestions.

It is also likely that some names that break
rules names can be
generated. That a name came from the name generator does not
give it a free pass from rules
names or help
namechange.




      See also:


      NAMES, ROLEPLAY

title: NEWBIE, NEWCOMER, WELCOME
body:
I. Introduction

MUME is an open world game based on J. R.
R. Tolkien's creation, Middle-earth. Within the game you
will find familiar places such as
Rivendell, the Shire, and
Bree. You will find less welcome figures like Bill Ferny,
Old Man Willow, and even Sauron. You may
even find more mysterious people; Beorn, Galadriel, and
Tom Bombadil.


  II. Starting the Game

If you are a new player just starting off, you may be confused as to where you
are and how to leave. The place you are in is called the
Halls of Mandos. This is the place to where all
new characters of the good races
start off, and is also where Arda's fallen heroes go to
recover when they have been slain.

The only way to leave the Halls of Mandos is by
praying to a destination. New players are recommended to
begin in the Tower Hills, which offers inexperienced
adventurers a large number of quests to familiarize them
with the game's mechanics. To leave your starting room for the
Tower Hills, type: pray to
the tower hills

Before leaving your start room, please read this
help file entirely. Many of the questions you will have
are covered in the FAQ's and they will hopefully
save you a lot of confusion.


  III. The Help System

The text you are reading now is part of the extensive set of
help pages which has been carefully written and updated to
help new players and old. Simply type
help with no arguments for a list of available
commands and help topics. All of the
commands in these help pages are
easily identifiable and have their own help page that you
can read. All you need to do is type
help <command> which will
give more information: for example, help
newcomer which is this help article.


  IV. Playing the Game

What you do after you have prayed to the Tower Hills
is up to you. You can decide to solve quests to gain
experience (help
quest), explore the world to gain
travel points (help
map), or chat with the friendly
community on global communication
channels (help
narrate).

A recommended goal for any new player is to reach level 13
where they graduate newcomer-hood and drastically increase the depth and
challenge of the game. Graduation unlocks the evil races
for your account allowing you to play an
Orc, Troll, or Black
Númenórean. These
races are on the opposite side of the war, are considerably
harder to master, and have their own separate global
communication channel.


  V. Where to find Answers

If you ever get lost, can not find something, or need further
information, you can ask other players
by typing questions like narrate Hello! Any advice
for new players?. To find the
names of players who you're chatting
with on your side within MUME, you can type
who. To find a little information about any of the people that you
see listed or in person type whois
<name>, an example being whois
manwe. Type help tell, help
say for more information on communicating with other
players. Our larger community is also available on
Discord with details to join at help
discord.

Related help subjects are also mentioned in the 'See also'
part at the bottom of help files. You can always type
help <topic> to find out more.
For example, you can type help faq to
read summaries about basic MUME
commands and features. The
FAQ help file is also available on the
MUME web site at
https://mume.org/help/faq

We hope this text could give you a few
hints on how to start and where you can get the answers you
need.




      See also:


      BASICS, FAQ1,
      FAQ2, FAQ3,
      FAQ4, FAQ5,
      ADVANCED, FEATURES,
      RULES, PRAY

body:
Syntax      : cast 'night vision'
Type        : Detection
Accumulative: No
Duration    : Yes
Casting     : Normal
Position    : Standing
Level       : Level 7
Class       : Magic User
Min. Mana   : 25

This spell will allow you to see players and
objects in a room that would otherwise be hidden by
darkness. The duration is dependent on how powerful a
caster you are.

To master this skill, a brilliant mind, deep insight and good eyesight are
required.

Example:

  > cast 'night vision'





      See also:


      DETECT MAGIC,
      DETECT INVISIBILITY

title: NARRATE, SHOUT, TALES
body:
If you want to tell a tale to most other
players in the game, narrate it. All the
players wanting to hear such things will receive it and
all the players who don't want to be disturbed won't. You
can choose to receive tales from other players using the
command listen tales.

These communication channels
are not completely global, as they are restricted to either
players of the same race, or at least
to players of the same side of the war between Good and
Evil.

The narrate channel is meant primarily for in-game
communication. Discussions about music, movies,
computers, sports and other RL related issues generally don't belong there.

If you are asked by other player(s) to take your discussion to the
songs channel, you are required to do so.

shout is an alias for narrate.
The output of narrate is influenced by the comprehension
level of the language that is
being used.

Example:

  > narrate Is it safe to travel from Bree to Fornost?





      See also:


      TELL, YELL,
      LISTEN, SING,
      IGNORE

title: NIGHTMARES, SLEEP
body:
The sleep command will simply put you to sleep.

Example:

  > sleep


You will automatically wake up if someone hits you, or if
you have a frightful nightmare!

While sleeping you regenerate hit points,
movement points, and mana
faster.

Sleeping next to a campfire or a
comfortable bed provides a minor
regeneration boost.




      See also:


      WAKE





  The spell


Syntax      : cast 'sleep' <character>
Type        : Offensive, mental
Accumulative: No
Duration    : Yes
Casting     : Extremely long
Position    : Standing
Level       : Level 14
Class       : Magic User
Min. Mana   : 15

If an intended victim fails to resist this spell, he is put to magical sleep
for a long time. As long as somebody is being affected by this powerful
enchantment, he cannot wake up unless being physically
injured.

To master this skill, a brilliant mind and an iron will are required.

Example:

  > cast 'sleep' olog

title: NOLDOR
body:
The division of the Elves that followed Finwë as their
lord. In the long march from Cuiviénen to the western shores of
Middle-earth, they were second great host. When they reached Valinor, they
learned much from Aulë the Smith, and were accounted the greatest of the
Elves in matters of lore and craft.

They dwelt in Aman for many Ages, but after the Darkening of Valinor many of
the Noldor (S. Golodhrim) forsook the Undying Lands and followed Melkor to
Middle-earth. Melkor had slain Finwë and stolen the Silmarils, the work of
Fëanor, the greatest craftsman of that people, and the Noldor returned to
make war on him until he gave up the Great Jewels.


  MUME Noldor

MUME's Noldor Elves have several
bonuses. These include:



    They have a natural sensitivity to magic, and have a
    natural passive ability like the
    Detect Magic spell.


    They have access to a quest that will allow them to
    add a minor gem socket to a focus.





      See also:


      ELVES

title: NEW
body:
If you are new to MUME, or MUDs in general, it is
recommended that you read the following
help texts (by typing
help <help text name>):

When reading a help file, check out the "See also"

      HELP NEWCOMER

      HELP BASICS

      HELP FAQ3

title: NOQUIT, UNABLE TO QUIT
body:
When you attack someone else or are attacked by someone
else your ability to quit the game
or rent in an inn is suspended for a
certain amount of time:


    about two minutes if you fought a mobile


    more if you were involved in player versus player conflict


If your link drops while you are affected by unable to
quit (as shown by the stat command),
other players will still be able to damage you while you
are unable to quit.

Moreover, if you are a Troll and lose
link while you are unable to quit, you are vulnerable to
sundeath.




      See also:


      RENT, QUIT,
      NOVOID

title: NEWS
body:
The news command lets you read important news
about the game, as posted on News of Arda boards.
You don't have to stand at such a
board to use the news command.


Syntax:
  news [all|whole|next|[tail] <number>]




      news


      displays the news board (like l
      board)




      news all (or whole)


      displays the whole news board (like l w
      b)




      news next


      displays the next unread message (like read
      next)




      news <number>


      displays the message <number> (like
      read <num>)




      news reset


      mark all news messages as unread




      news search <text>


      search for <text> in news messages




      news tail


      displays the latest news messages




      news tail <number>


      displays the <number> latest news messages




      news catchup


      Mark all messages as read.




      news catchup <number>


      Mark all news messages up to message
      <number> as read.




      news catchup -<number>


      Mark all messages except the last
      <number> as read.




Make sure to read game news as it appears. They may contain
important information and rule changes.

Example:

  > news reset
  > news catchup -12
  > news

News are archived after a RL year: these entries will not be listed in
news and will be displayed last by news next. See
help board for more information.

You can also receive the latest news via the RSS
feed.




      See also:


      READ, VIEW,
      BOARDS, RSS

title: NOSHOUT, NOTELL
body:
Players who abuse their
communication commands (for
example, by narrating dozens of times within a few seconds, or singing
offensive things) can be NO-SHOUTED by the Ainur.
A no-shouted character cannot send or receive global
communications (pray, narrate, and
sing).

Players who abuse the
tell command receive instead a NO-TELL
flag. This prevents them from using tell to
harass other players.

title: NOTE, PEN, WRITE
body:
In order to write a note, you need a piece of blank paper (often available at
your local grocer) and a quill pen. You need to
hold the pen and then write note.
To read the note, you need to
hold the note and read
note.

To write a message on a bulletin board, use
write <subject> in the room where the
board is. You may also want to
reply to the last message you
read.

This command will take you into your chosen editor (from
change editor). For the standard line
editor, you may exit by entering
%e on a new line.




      See also:


      READ, BOARDS,
      MAIL, PIGEON,
      MARK, EDITOR

title: NOIDEA
body:
These are ideas which have been considered by the MUME
management (in this case principally the
Implementors) and ruled to never appear as long as
they draw breath:


  Races



    Ents, wargs or horses as player
    characters


    Orcs with teleport capability or
    any spell that they had prior to introduction of shaman
    class


    Trolls having mounts


    Trolls without sundeath


    Trolls not accidentally fleeing into sunlight


    Trolls being able to hide,
    sneak, or cast
    spells


    Trolls with shops (that can do
    anything but mending)


    BNs with a city


    BNs with a warrior guild master


    Evil characters being able to become immortal



  Classes



    Additional class-dependent skills. The move is away
    from unique abilities for classes and towards
    racial-modifiers of
    abilities/skills.



  Levels and Skills



    Experience for casting healing
    spells


    A means of transferring exp to tp/wp or vice-versa


    A spell for transferring hps to mana


    Bashing someone removing or delaying their autoflee


    WPs or scalps required to level



  Equipment



    Being able to buy heals or healing
    spells from clerical-mobiles


    Banks and places to store excess
    equipment


    A perfect or even near-playable system for firing into adjacent rooms


    Critical hits negated by armour


    Level-dependent equipment



  General



    Splitting MUME in two (or more) games (+/-pk,
    +/-Tolkien, etc)


    An auction channel


    Safe areas where newbies can learn
    commands


    Any game effect which relies on the
    noquit or
    novoid flags. They exist solely for
    linkdrop/rent.


    Having anything on noidea removed (Unless the
    idea of removal was thought of by an
    Implementor)


    Removal of the entire noidea list. (This is so much a
    noidea it needs 2 Implementors to agree
    on it, so not much chance of that)


    Implementation of the superidea, or any similar forms, which
    by nature, would act to supersede the noidea category





      See also:


      CONTRIBUTING

title: NOVOID, UNABLE TO VOID
body:
MUME characters have
linkless protection: if your link
drops, you soon become invulnerable until you reconnect.

The mechanism that prevents abuse of linkless protection
is called novoid. If you meet (or engage, scry,
hear, etc.) an enemy, novoid is enabled for a period of time. The
stat command will list you as unable to
void.

While you have novoid, you can rent at an
inn normally: it only affects your vulnerability while you
are linkless. It does not determine whether you
get a mob- or a PK-death should you die.

If you are already linkless, you cannot become
novoid.




      See also:


      NOQUIT

title: NÍNUI, SOLMATH
fieldBlock:
Dawn   9 am
Dusk   5 pm
body:
Dawn   9 am
Dusk   5 pm




      See also:


      MONTHS

title: OFFER, RENT, TRADE
body:
Renting and Offers

At an innkeeper, the offer command will
make it tell you the cost of storing your carried
items (and money) for one real life
day.

rent will store the items
and make you leave the game.

The next time you enter, you'll start out in the inn where
you left. The inn will store your
items as long as you have the gold to
pay the rent. Money will be automatically taken out of
moneybags to cover the expense.


  Costs, Confiscation, and Recovery

For playability reasons, rent costs are not linear in time and rent cost is
greatly reduced for equipped items. The first
day of rent costs more than the second, which costs more than
the third, and so on. As a consequence, players who can't
connect for a few weeks won't have to pay an exorbitant sum when they
return. Items in your
inventory or containers cost more.

If you overstay at an inn and you don't have enough
money to pay the rent, your
equipment is confiscated to cover
the cost. However, innkeepers will give you the opportunity
to recover your possessions, provided that you pay them
the money owed - plus a penalty fee. It is recommended you
repay your debt as soon as possible, as your former possessions will be sold
off 24 RL hours after.

You cannot recover equipment you
lost due to link-rent and you need an innkeeper to
recover items - which means
Black Númenóreans and
Zaugurz Orcs cannot
recover their confiscated
equipment.

The status of the confiscated equipment can be checked
with the offer command. To recover it,
give the exact amount requested to the
innkeeper.


  Restrictions

Players above level 15 (other than
Istari) will not be able to rent in some towns as the folk
there are simply too suspicious of them. Evil high level
players will have to risk going to the forsaken city of
Tharbad, while good players should
journey to places such as the fair Rivendell.


  Renting Pets and Mounts

You can also use the rent command to rent your
mobiles (e.g., horses) at
stables. Move to a stable, and type
rent <pet> (for example,
rent horse) in order to do this. You have to
lead or ride the
mobile you want to rent.

You can retrieve your mobile from the
stables by using the trade command to
return the ticket and get your
mobile back.


  Warning about Link-rent

If your connection to the game breaks, after a while the game will rent you
automatically. Note that most of the time this will result in you paying much
greater rent costs. You will also be rented automatically if the game crashes
or reboots.


  Cheaper rent for ancient
  characters

Ancient characters of the good
races are expected to live peacefully and thus pay a lower
rent in a few inns: free, cheaper or normal, according to
their current wealth.




      See also:


      CAMP, INNS,
      NOQUIT, LINK,
      HOMETOWNS, ANCIENT,
      STABLES

title: ORCS, SNAGA
body:
Also known as Goblins, these foul creatures were created by Morgoth in the
First Age. Through his evil power, it is said he corrupted the beautiful
Elves and transformed them into his servants of evil, the
Orcs. They delight in seeing things suffer and bear malice
especially to Elves and Dwarves. They
are not intelligent and gain most of their destructive power in their large
clans. The evil force of Mordor has drawn Orcs together to create a force along
with His other servants which is maybe too strong for the
Elves and Men to vanquish.


  MUME Orcs

MUME Orcs are very strong, but other than that suffer
considerably. Orcs make powerful warriors, but have difficulties with other
classes.

There are three tribes of Orcs in MUME; the
Uruk-Tarkhnarb,
Uruk-Morruhk, and the
Uruk-Zaugurz. The Tarkhnarb
and Morruhk Orcs are subjects of
Sauron, allies of the Black
Númenóreans and the powerful Trolls in
the battle against the Free People. The Zaugurz Orcs were
cast out of Goblin Gate (the primary
dwelling of the Tarkhnarb), and are now at war with the
Tarkhnarb and their allies.

Orcs in MUME are treated differently from the other
races:



    They may not become immortal.


    They generally have worse stats than the other
    races.


    Sunlight affects them badly (much lower bonuses, use
    movement points much faster, increased
    difficulty in spell casting).


    They have the ability to see in the dark without a
    light source.


Players or mobiles might refer to
orcs as "snagas" at times.




      See also:


      RACES, TARKHNARB,
      ZAUGURZ, MORRUHK

title: OOC, OUT OF CHARACTER
body:
OOC simply means Out of Character, and a player can use the term to indicate he
goes from IC (In Character) to OOC,
thus not roleplaying anymore.

This is just a term, and not a command (yet).




      See also:


      IC, COMMENT,
      ROLEPLAYING

title: ORDER
body:
Use order to order a pet or a charmed person to
do something. For example:


  > order cat say I speak animal!
  The Cat says 'R fsiedaamimal!'


  > order followers smile  [Order all charmed followers]


Note that it is not possible to order mobiles to do any
of the following commands:
narrate, yell,
shout, tell, sing,
pray and beep. There are no restrictions
on what commands other players can
be ordered to perform though.




      See also:


      COMMAND, CHARM

title: PALANTÍR, PALANTÍRI
body:
PALANTÍR, PALANTÍRI


             Tall ships and tall kings
             Three times three,
             What brought they from the foundered land
             Over the flowing sea?
             Seven stars and seven stones
             And one white tree.

The seven stones were also known as the Palantíri and they were used by
the Númenóreans to communicate across
vast distances. It is said that the stones were kept at Minas Ithil, Osgiliath,
Minas Tirith, Orthanc, Amon Sûl, Annúminas and the
Tower Hills.

After the fall of the north kingdom knowledge of those stones faded from mortal
minds and the sight of the stewards of Gondor was dimmed in the north.

They were solid spheres appearing when at rest to be made of
solid glass or crystal deep black in hue. At smallest they were about a foot in
diameter, but some, certainly the stones of Amon Sûl and Osgiliath were
much larger and could not be lifted by one man. They were
very heavy and unbreakable by any violence then controlled by
men.

Alone the palantíri could only "see:" they did not transmit
sound. Ungoverned by a directing mind they were wayward and their visions
(apparently at least) haphazard.

After the fall of Minas Ithil to the forces of Sauron the
knowledge of that palantír was also lost to the forces of good.




      See also:


      "Unfinished Tales" by JRRT.

title: PANIC
body:
If you flee out of combat (as opposed
to making an ordered retreat using the escape
command) you may be affected by panic for a short time.

When you are in a state of panic you will find that your
offensive abilities are reduced. Though the durations
of multiple panics are not cumulative, their effects on your
ability to fight are.

title: PARRY
body:
(Warrior Skill)

Even though the most important thing in combat might be to
kill your enemy fast, knowing how to defend yourself is also important. By
knowing how to parry blows you will indeed live longer, and maybe it will win
the fight for you since parrying gives you more time to hit and less time to
bleed.

Great agility, good eyesight and lots of muscle are quite important when
learning this.

Learning this skill will improve your parrying bonus with given
equipment. After a certain increase in your skill
percentage, your basic parrying bonus will increase a given amount.

Your parrying bonus (PB) will be divided among attackers.




      See also:


      DODGE

title: PERCEPTION
body:
Perception is a base ability. It measures all of a
character's senses, with an emphasis on eyesight,
hearing and smell. It is essential in discovering hidden things (such as
someone waiting in ambush), in following tracks, when spotting gaps in an
opponent's armour to strike at, and in taking aim for
long-range attacks.




      See also:


      STATISTICS

title: PIERCING, PIERCING WEAPONS
body:
(Thief Skill) (Weapon
Class)

The piercing weapons skill applies to all kinds of daggers, knives and similar
- if they are wielded in one hand only.

Piercing weapons are all small and light-weight stabbers and piercers: daggers,
knives, rapiers and similar weapons. Their main
strength is their light
weight and flexibility, making it possible to hit more
often than with any other type of weapon. They don't do
much damage compared to heavier weapons, but they are
decent when it comes to defense. Also if you plan to sneak
up and backstab an opponent, it will only be possible
with a very small weapon, a piercer.

It takes great agility to master this skill; good eyesight and lots of muscle
are important too.




      See also:


      ATTACK, BACKSTAB,
      CHARGE, CLEAVING,
      CONCUSSION, STABBING,
      SLASHING, TWO-HANDED

title: PAT
body:
The pat command is a normal social, but it
also allows you to pat objects.




      See also:


      SOCIALS

title: PIPE, SMOKE
body:
If you have a pipe, you can try to smoke it by putting, for example, pipe-weed
into it. To smoke it, you have to hold your
pipe and then smoke.

Note: If you rest before smoking
pipe-weed you may feel more focused!

title: PKILLING, PLAYER KILLING, PLAYERKILLING
body:
Player killing, or PK, means involving in combat and
trying to kill other player-controlled characters.




      See also:


      DEATH, "RULES PK",
      "RULES SAURON"

title: PICK
body:
(Thief Skill) [Delayed
Command]

Use the pick command to pick locks. Not all locks can be picked.

It is wise to make sure the lock is locked first. If you
attempt to pick a lock that is actually unlocked, there is a
chance you manage to lock it.

Having lockpicks improve your chances at picking. Also,
rumour has it that several people in Arda can improve your
lockpicks — at a price.

Most people have the misconception that picking locks are for criminals and the
like only. Many heroic adventurers have gotten stuck outside that locked old
door in an abandoned tower, or blocked from infinite
treasures by a rusty old padlock. Of course, also burglars pick locks.

It takes a brilliant mind to master this skill, and it helps to have great
agility.

Examples:

  > pick door north
  > pick oakdoor
  > pick hiddensafe

You can also pick fruit and other plants:

  > pick apple





      See also:


      OPEN, CLOSE,
      LOCK, UNLOCK,
      "BREAK DOOR", BASH

title: POINT
body:
With the point command, you can point in a direction, at an
exit, an object or a
character:


  > point north
  > point door east
  > point elf
  > point sword

title: PORTAL
fieldBlock:
Syntax      : cast 'portal' <room key>
Type        : Long range
Accumulative: No
Duration    : Yes
Casting     : Extremely long
Position    : Standing
Level       : Level 18
Class       : Magic User
Min. Mana   : 90
body:
Syntax      : cast 'portal' <room key>
Type        : Long range
Accumulative: No
Duration    : Yes
Casting     : Extremely long
Position    : Standing
Level       : Level 18
Class       : Magic User
Min. Mana   : 90

This is a very powerful spell which may be used to make a temporary connection
between two locations far removed from each another. It has a limited range and
cannot be used within city terrain.

The spell requires an identification of the destination, which you can get by
any locate spell.

While the portal is open, anyone can enter
portal and get magically transported to the other side.

It takes a brilliant mind to master this spell, and it helps to have an iron
will.

Example:

  > cast 'portal' yaleque





      See also:


      TELEPORT, LOCATE,
      LOCATE LIFE

title: PET
body:
In certain towns and home areas there are places (pet
shops) where one may purchase animals. You might be able to
buy horses as well as pigeons, cats, and
dogs. For example:





> buy horse






> buy horse Shadowfax



      also gives your pet a name




Pets can be useful in many ways. For instance, you can order them
to assist you in battle, help you carry
more over long distances, or even send messages over long distances for certain
pets like pigeons!




      See also:


      RULES CHANNELS, HELP
      COMMAND, ORDER,
      CHARM, PIGEON

title: POUR
body:
Use pour to transfer a liquid from one
container to another.

Syntax:




pour <source> <destination>






pour <source> out



      this empties <source>




Examples:





          pour water cup




      works if there is a water source in the room





> pour fountain skin






Note: If you want to fill a
lantern with oil, use the
fill command.




      See also:


      DRINK, EMPTY

title: PIGEON
body:
If you wish to send a small item - usually a note - to someone else, you can
buy a trained pigeon in a pet
shop or find one wandering the wilds.

First you may need to train the pigeon, and
then use send to fly off with whatever it is
carrying:

Examples:

  > train pigeon
  > give note pigeon
  > send bilbo

Note: that occasionally pigeons may get lost and neither deliver the
item, nor come back to the owner.




      See also:


      ORDER

title: PRACTICE
body:
[Instant Command]

In order to progress in MUME, you will need to
practice skills. When you begin the game you
will be given a number of "practice sessions," which may be used in
any guild. As you gain levels, you are
also awarded more sessions.

The results of practicing a skill will depend on your
class. One session is always required to practice in any
guild, however, the practices needed to further your
knowledge of skills is slower when you practice
skills not tied to your class. For
example, if a thief with the same stats
as a warrior practices the skill
"parry" once he will spend
1 practice but gain around the half the
knowledge the warrior would - to gain the same %
knowledge as the warrior, the thief
must spend 2 practice sessions.

Each time you practice a given skill, your efficiency (%) will increase. You
can see your current efficiency as a percentage by using the Practice command
with no argument. This will also show what
skills you may practice, when you are in a
guild.

Some skills are easier or harder to
learn than others in the same group
(the % increase will be quicker or slower). The gain in knowledge in a skill
per practice session is also related to your stats - note
that only unmodified (natural) stats are considered for
practicing purposes. That is, the stats unaffected by age,
spells and equipment.

When you learn a skill outside your
class, this skill will be less efficient than for a
character of that class. For
example, a level 20
mage using backstab will be as
proficient as a
level 13
thief. Here is the correspondence table for effective
levels used for skills:
1 -> 100%,
2 -> 83%,
3 -> 67%,
4 -> 50%.

Practice sessions are cumulative. If you don't want to
learn any skills at a certain
level, they will be carried on to the next
level where you can use them, if you wish. This is
especially useful for spell casters, as they receive access to new
spells as they gain levels.

You can decay practice points in skills. Each time you
forget some knowledge in a skill, you will regain one practice
point. For more information see help
train.

It is also possible to relearn a skill that has decayed by asking another
character to teach you — see
help learn.

Since skills can decay, practice resets will not
be given under any circumstances. However, retired people can get a practice
reset after 30 days.
help retire will provide complete details.

Examples:

  > practice
  > practice ride




      See also:


      CLASS, GUILD,
      LEARN, RETIRE,
      TRAIN

title: PRONOUNCIATION
body:
This is a general guide to pronunciation of words (particularly
names) in languages. However, since
the majority of words are in Sindarin and Quenya, there is a noticeable bias to
describing the intonations.

Specialist guides for pronunciation of individual
languages may well follow as part
of a overview of each language: Quenya, Sindarin,
Adûnaic, Khuzdul, Valarin, Black Speech and Orkish.

The intended purpose of this guide is to help you in
pronouncing words that you may well encounter, as well
as an aid to choosing an appropriate sounding name for your
race.


  Stress

In the Eldarin languages, stress is indicated by the
form of the word, and as a general rule, it applies also in
other tongues. Stress is shown here merely by capitalising the vowel in
question.

In words of two syllables, the stress falls on the first.

Example: Orome

In words of three or more syllables, it falls on the penultimate syllable when
that syllable contains a long vowel, a diphthong, or a vowel followed by more
than one consonant.

Examples: IsIldur, elentÁri, periAnnath,
silIvren

In words of three or more syllables where the penultimate syllable is a short
vowel followed by at most one consonant, the stress
falls on the syllable before.

Examples: erEssëa (last e short), fËanor, ancAlima, ecthElion,
pelArgir

Note that in Sindarin the following should be considered as single
consonants: ch, dh, th.

Example: nImbrethil (not nimbrEthil), dEnethor (not denEthor)

Other languages have their own
consonant clusters which are treated as single
consonants when considering stress, but are not
discussed here.




      See also:


      VOWELS, CONSONANTS

title: POSITION, REST, SIT, STAND, WAKE
body:
The following commands are used to change your
position.

If you feel weary, it is probably a good idea to
sit or rest for a while; or maybe even take a nap
with the sleep command.

Resting on benches, beds, straw pallets, and other such provide a minor boost
to regeneration.

Examples:

  > rest
  > sleep
  > wake
  > stand

Use change prompt position to toggle
whether you show your position (as a number) in your
prompt.




      See also:


      PROMPT

title: PULL, PUSH
body:
In some places there are things you can try to push and pull.

Example:

  > pull lever
  > push stone

title: PUT
body:
For putting objects in containers. Note that the
in, in the examples, is optional.

Examples:




      put the dagger in the bag




      put all in bag


      put everything (except the bag) in the bag




      put all.bread bag


      put all objects of a certain type in a
      container




      put sword room.sack


      put sword in the first sack in room




      put 3 gold sack


      money should be in <amount>
      <unit> format; note that Elves have
      different names for money




In addition, put on is an alias for
wear and put down is an
alias for drop:




      put on red-shoes


      … and dance the blues




      put down sack


      drop your sack







      See also:


      GET, DROP, WEAR,
      MONEY, SPECIFYING
      OBJECTS

title: PRAY
body:
In the Halls of Mandos, this command is used to
transport yourself to one of the main towns and cities of Middle-earth. New
players are recommended to begin in the
Tower Hills. Alternatively, experienced
players may choose to pray to their "racial
home":




      Elves, Half-elves


      the Grey Havens,
      Lórien, Rivendell




      Men


      Fornost, Tharbad




      Dwarves


      the Blue Mountains




      Hobbits


      the Shire (Hobbiton)




      Bears


      the Anduin Vale




You do not have to pray to the town populated by your race.
However, when you are in a city populated by your own kind, you have some
advantages, such as prices for things being cheaper to you. Everyone can pray
to Bree but this is not recommended for newcomers. Only evil
humans may pray to Tharbad and various other restrictions
also apply.



    Among the mentioned places, the Tower
    Hills is the best area to explore for new adventurers; being
    situated right between the realms of dwarves,
    elves, hobbits, and
    men.


    The Shire is the most peaceful. Travellers in
    the Shire are able to wander far with little chance of
    danger (or adventure!).


    Fornost is fairly dangerous, many dangerous
    creatures fill the woods around it, and
    Orcs and worse may raid the lands about.


    The village of Bree is very similar to
    Fornost, and sooner or later everyone has to travel
    to Bree. You will have to be more cautious than in the
    area of the Grey Havens, since
    orcs have been spotted recently.


    The woods around the Dwarven city of the Blue
    Mountains are also perilous, but the bold
    dwarf venturing into them may make his fortune
    mining.


    The lands around the Grey Havens of the
    Elves are less dangerous than those about
    Fornost or the Blue
    Mountains, but more perilous than the Shire.


    Elves also have the possibility to start in
    Lórien, which is quite safe, but
    anyone living there is trapped in the east and the journey into the west is
    far and very dangerous!


    Furthermore, elves can pray to
    Rivendell. Yet, since many dangerous
    places lie near this elven stronghold and it is said numerous strong
    heroes of the west have been slain by fearsome
    trolls and dreadful orcs in the
    last time, this place is not suited for the inexperienced adventurer.


    Beorning Men and
    Bears may pray to the Anduin Vale. It is
    treacherous, many fearsome creatures wander Mirkwood Forest, and
    Orcs from Goblin-town prowl its perimeter.


    Praying to Tharbad is better left to those
    who really know what they are doing!


The first time you pray, or if you have no citizenships for any other reason,
you may pray only to the hometowns for your
race, and will be made a citizen of
that place. Note that "praying to a city" only works in the
Halls of Mandos and nowhere else.


The other function of the pray command is to send a message to all
immortals that are logged on. This is thus a rather
powerful command and you should not use it unless the issue is important and
only immortals can solve it. For instance, if you can
ask a visible immortal via tell and get
the necessary response, this is considered far better than simply praying.

By the same reasoning, immortals should not use pray as
a replacement for tell.

The policy for prayers are that the mortal should indicate what the problem is
in his prayer:

Good prays:


    may I have a newbie kit?


    my strength suddenly decreased from 17 to 1, what's
    up?


    Morgul blade disappeared, but it was
    Sauron's darkness.


    Fornost warrior
    guild isn't working.


Bad prays:


    I need to speak with a V+ please?


    may I speak to a god?


    I have a problem.


    Can someone help me?


The point again: the pray should include enough information
to say what the problem is, not what person you
would like to talk to.

Example:

  > pray Harry won't open the gate for me, although I'm a citizen





      See also:


      NARRATE, SING

title: QUESTS
body:
A number of quests of varying complexity are available within the game. You can
find quests by walking around, keeping your eyes open and
talking to NPCs that look interested in talking with you.
Quests may be repeatable, timed, and some even failed.

You can keep track of your active and completed quests by
using your Quest Log. As you find more and more
characters that require your aid in various matters,
you will take notes that you can reference in the future in case you forget
what you're trying to accomplish.

You can list the areas that you have quests in with quests:


  > quests
  You have learnt of quests in the following areas:
  Eriador    Fangorn  Lórien

You can list the quests in an area with quests
<area>. The area names may be
abbreviated for convenience:


  > quests eriador
  You have learnt of the following quests in Eriador:
    snake hunt  - Exterminate slithering snakes in the Tower Hills

This will list your quests in Eriador where, in this example, 'snake hunt' is
the quest name. You can then read the
info about a specific quest with quests
<name>. You can also use quests
<name> in <area> in case there are quests
and areas with similar names.

Examples:

  > quests snake hunt
  > que snake hu
  > q sn hu in eri

All the above examples display the quest 'snake hunt' in the 'Eriador' area.

Note: Some failed quests may be attempted again immediately while
others requires the NPC to forget about you, which may take
a very long time.




      See also:


      ACHIEVEMENTS, HISTORY

title: PROTECTION FROM EVIL
fieldBlock:
Syntax      : cast 'protection from evil'
Type        : Defensive
Accumulative: No
Duration    : Yes
Casting     : Normal
Position    : Standing
Level       : Level 4
Class       : Cleric
Min. Mana   : 20
body:
Syntax      : cast 'protection from evil'
Type        : Defensive
Accumulative: No
Duration    : Yes
Casting     : Normal
Position    : Standing
Level       : Level 4
Class       : Cleric
Min. Mana   : 20

While affected by this warding spell creatures of evil will hesitate before
attacking you - such is the nature of this magical incantation - thus perhaps
giving you time to get away or even maybe slay the foul beast before it dares
engage you.

Deep insight and an iron will are quite important when learning this.

Example:


  > cast 'protection from evil'

title: PROTECT
body:
The protect command is used to select a number of people
(players or mobiles) that you will
try to protect from attacks.

When someone tries to hit one of those in your "protected list", you
get an attempt to intercept the blow. The chance to succeed depends on how high
you know the rescue skill.

If you have more than one person on your list, or if you already are
fighting, your chance to succeed is lowered. If the
person to be protected knows the escape skill, the chance
of success improves. If the person to be protected is in the same
group as the person attacking then you will not intercept
the blow.

Only physical attacks (hit, bash
and kick) are affected by this command.

Examples:

  protect             lists who you will try to protect
  protect frodo       toggles whether you will try to protect Frodo or not
  protect myself      clears the list of people you will protect




      See also:


      RESCUE

title: PURSUE
body:
[Delayed Command]

If you find a track using the command
track
<target>, you have the option to
follow these tracks with the command pursue.
pursue will cause you to follow the
track in whichever direction it leads. This is a faster and
more convenient way to follow a track
over long distances.

Also note that pursue will cause you to enter the room in question
no matter what danger may lie in it. You will need to enter the command each
time you wish to pursue your victim.

You can also pursue <target>.
This command has the same delay as track
<target> but will also move you when
you find the track. It can be used for initial tracking but
is not advisable as a method of following a track over
longer distances.

Examples:

  > pursue
  > pursue gwokk

For following a track over several rooms:

  > track *dwarf*  OR  pursue *dwarf*
  > pursue
  > pursue




      See also:


      TRACK

Five of these belong to the good side. They are Men,

title: PUNISH
body:
Since people are in different time zones and what not, the game has a system to
allow players who have been imprisoned and accused of
rule-breaking to automatically appeal or accept their punishment.

If a player chooses to accept their punishment, they will be automatically
released from prison (Morgul Vale).
Players with pending punishments must log in their
imprisoned characters before they can resume normal
gameplay.

To address pending punishments, players need to log in
with their imprisoned character and use the following
commands:




      punish list


      Lists all pending punishments




      punish appeal


      Write an appeal against the punishment




      punish accept


      Accept the punishment and be released from prison







      See also:


      RULES

title: RAISE, RAISE EYEBROWS, RAISE HANDS
body:
The raise command is like a normal social
with a minor twist. You can either raise or raise
hand which will raise one hand, you can raise hands to
raise two hands, raise eyebrow to raise an eyebrow, or raise
eyebrows to raise both eyebrows.




      See also:


      SOCIALS

title: REBOOT, REBOOT DAEMON, REBOOT DEMON
body:
Every once in a while MUME will need to reboot to
incorporate new features as well as to change or update
certain game functions. A reboot usually takes about 30 seconds.

Periodically, the game is also rebooted to "clean up" the world. Some
features of the game are not well adapted to the game
never being restarted.

Any mount you were riding/leading at
the time of reboot will disappear so it might be a good idea
to rent it at your local
stable. Also, if you do not plan on coming back to the
game immediately after the reboot be aware that the cost of renting your
characters outside of an inn is
considerably higher.

During a reboot the world will return to its default
status. Doors will close; hostile
creatures will pop up; anything that you may have left on the ground (and
possibly some rare items you may have acquired) will vanish
forever. Contrarily to what happens during a crash, after a
reboot you reappear wherever you were - or in the close
proximity. So, even if you do not want to rent, it is wise
to move to a safe place before MUME reboots.

The Aratar can reboot the game at any time and for any
reason.




      See also:


      RENT, OFFER,
      CRASH, SHUTDOWN

body:
Just to prevent you from accidental quitting.

This command doesn't do anything, it simply is.

If you really want to quit (and not
rent), type all of
quit.

title: REBORN
body:
[Instant Command] (Troll only)

Trolls who sundie can choose whether to have their
trophy cleared (thereby losing the list of pkills of their
previous life) or not.

Other things will also reset, such as
achievements,
herblore knowledge, and
quest progress.

If you died to what looks like a bug, don't use the
reborn command, or the Valar won't be able to
reimburse you.

Note: You can only use the reborn command to obtain a
trophy reset if you are a newly
sundead troll without any
experience or travel
points.




      See also:


      SUNDEATH, TROLL

Position    : Standing
Level       : Level 18
Class       : Shaman

body:
Syntax      : cast 'raise dead' <corpse>
Type        : Miscellaneous
Accumulative: No
Duration    : Yes
Casting     : Extremely long
Position    : Standing
Level       : Level 18
Class       : Shaman
Min. Mana   : 50

This spell will find the target
corpse present in the room where it is
cast and raise a
shadow from that corpse, provided
that the living being was sufficiently intelligent; otherwise the
shadow raised will dissolve. If the
shadow is suitably powerful, it will even
follow you. Only one shadow of this

To master this spell, deep insight and an iron will are required.

Example:

  > cast 'raise dead' 2.corpse

title: RECITE, SCROLLS
body:
[Delayed Command]

Syntax:

  recite <scroll> [<target>]


Is used to "read" a magical scroll. The
<target> can be an
object, character or nothing
(which may be yourself).

Note: You can for example use black-scroll or
blue-scroll to specify exactly which scroll to recite.

Examples:




> recite purple



      Recite a purple scroll on yourself





> recite purple-scroll



      Same effect





> recite black-scroll trix



      Recite a black scroll on Trix







      See also:


      CAST

title: RANGERS
body:
Rangers are heroes (level 21+) of the
free people of Arda who willingly help new
players out with questions and other things. A Ranger
(unlike Istari) has the right to deny a
newbie help and can also be fully
involved in the race wars. Rangers, however, are supposed
to set a good example among the heroes of the Free People,
and will hence be severely punished by Elbereth or the
Valar if he or she misbehaves.

Since being a ranger is a prolonged volunteer service, rangers can —
unlike the Istari — go
incognito. Rangers who have the 'who'
incognito flag set will not be shown under who
ranger.

To become a Ranger, contact any member of the management - to do so, just send
a tell to some visible V+ or pray once in
a while during playing. Rangers should be at least a hero
(level 21).




      See also:


      ISTARI

title: READ
body:
Obviously, this is used for reading things.

To read a message on a bulletin board, you have to
read its number; e.g., to read message 25: read 25.

To read the contents of a book or of a note, you might have to
hold it in your hands.




      See also:


      BOARDS, WRITE,
      MAIL, TAIL,
      LIBRARIES, MARK

Since some poisons are more powerful than others, they might take more than one

It takes deep insight to master this skill, and it helps to have a brilliant
mind.

Example:

  > cast 'remove poison'
  > cast 'remove poison' waterskin

title: REROLL
body:
If your character has been retired for more than 30
days, you will be able to use any available limited or full reroll. You can
check if you are eligible for a reroll by typing
account info
<name>. If you are, you will be able to reroll an
unlimited number of times until you leave retirement.
As part of rerolling your age will be reset and your
weight might change. You must use your rerolls before
leaving the Halls of Retirement or you will need to
retire for 30 days once again.


  Limited Rerolls

In limited rerolls, you can change a few of your unmodified
abilities from your reference
abilities, seen with info
%B, by a little - but not to make drastic changes, like turning a
spellcaster into a warrior.

Legend characters are only eligible to one limited
reroll every six months after the last time they used a
limited reroll.


  Full Rerolls

Full rerolls allow you to fully alter your reference
abilities.

All characters are only eligible to one full reroll
every four to eight years, depending on the
character's level, and after the
last time they used a full reroll. If you have never used a full reroll it
starts at the creation date of your character.

Examples:


  > account info frodo
  > reroll limited
  > reroll full

Note: As of NEWS 2666, rerolls are not dependent on
retirement time beyond the need to be retired for 30
days. You retain rerolls unless you use then.




      See also:


      ABILITIES, ACCOUNT,
      RETIRE, TRAIN,
      AGE RESET, PRAC RESET

title: RECOVER
body:
While wearing a quiver, bolt case or pouch for
slingstones, you can recover the
missiles lying around — those on the ground, the ones stuck in corpses
and the ones in your inventory. You will grab all the
missiles you shot or bought, and put them back in your quiver.

Note: In the above paragraph, inventory
includes any open containers found in your
inventory. Place missiles in a closed
container if you want to keep them from being
recovered.

You can also recover all; this will make you get all visible
missiles, no matter if they are yours or not.




      See also:


      AMMUNITION, SHOOT,
      ARCHERY, MISSILE
      WEAPONS

You can also specify a particular location:





> remove black finger

> remove from feet



      remove something from your feet





> remove all.pouch belt



      remove all pouches from your belt




The following wear positions exist:



      about


      anywhere


      asbelt


      belt


      feet


      hands


      held


      neck


      wield




      across


      arms


      back


      body


      finger


      head

      shield


      wrists







      See also:


      WEAR, WIELD





remove is also used to delete a message from
a bulletin board. Unless you are one of the
Ainur, you can only remove messages written by yourself.

Example:


  > remove 1046

      MAILBOX

title: RETROACTIVE RETIREMENT
body:
Characters who have been inactive for a year will be
automatically and retroactively retired. In other words, we'll pretend that
they anticipated their time away from MUME and properly
retired instead of renting.

Characters below legend level
will be auto deleted before that year has elapsed.

The players will be charged:


    1 year of rent if they were properly rented [1].


    Free rent if they had only very minimal
    equipment (like pants and a
    torch), even if they did not rent
    properly.


Characters who cannot afford that
rent or who are not in one of these situations (e.g., if
they dropped link with actual
equipment) will not be considered for retroactive
retirement.



    Note for legend home owners: the cost of the year of
    rent is computed from the offer you
    were given when renting. As the rent in a legend
    home is free, that rent will be free
    (but the upkeep will continue to elapse).


The purpose of this feature is to make it easier to
return to MUME if you forgot to
retire: these characters will be
eligible for an age reset, a limited
reroll, and a practice
reset. It shouldn't harm them in any
way.




      See also:


      RETIRE

title: REPLY
body:
The reply command is used to reply to the most recent message (a
tell, ask, or
whisper):


  Bilbo tells you 'bring the pipeweed'
  > reply I won't forget
  You tell Bilbo.


If you are standing at a bulletin board,
reply will instead reply to board messages:


  reply [quoted] [<number>] [by mail] [<title>]


If <number> is omitted (or replaced by some abbreviation of the
word last) you reply to the last message you
read.

If <title> is omitted your message will
have the title of the message you are replying to with
Re:  prepended to it.

If you include the word quoted, the messages you are replying to
will be included quoted using > .

If you write by mail, you
will instead send a private mail to the author. Example:





reply 123 by mail



      Reply to message 123 by mail





rep q b m



      Reply quoted to last message by mail





At a mailbox, reply instead replies to
mails.




      See also:


      MAILBOX, BOARDS,
      MARK, READ,
      TAIL, WRITE

title: REPOP, ZONE RESET
body:
Repop, zone reset

All the zones reset after some time has elapsed. How long
it will take, depends on the zone, and is typically between 20 - 60 minutes.

In general, when a zone resets, all of its contents are reloaded. This includes
mobiles, objects, and
doors for instance. Basically all of the content is
refreshed, but not every feature loads every time the
zone resets.

Note that mobs that were slain, may suddenly reappear. A
door that was opened, may suddenly
close and lock itself.

title: RETIRE, RETIREMENT
body:
There are two reasons for you to retire: a) to prevent auto deletion of your
character; and b) to obtain one of the three
resets/rerolls: a reroll, a
practice reset, or an
age reset.

In order to retire you must go to a receptionist and type
rent retire twice. When you type it once the
innkeeper will tell you how much
money you will have to pay; this sum equals 30 days of
normal rent. Once you have retired there will be no further
cost.

There are three restrictions that must be met to retire: you have at least one
item (such as a loaf of bread), at least 1 coin such as a
copper (a busc in the Elven tongue),
and enough money to pay your rent for 30
days.

Legend characters who have been inactive for a year
will be retroactively retired, see help
retroactive retirement.

To leave the retirement you use the leave command. Important: If
you leave before you do your
reroll,
pracreset, or
agereset you will not be able to use them
afterwards!

To make it perfectly clear: In case you want your resets you have to get them
while you are still retired and if you leave before doing them, you also will
not get a refund!

Some special notes:



    BNs can camp rent retire or retire at
    Karash (Dark Tower) and gaunt man.


    Low level retired characters
    might get deleted after long periods of inactiveness. While the details of
    this purging is not specific it is generally safe to assume that
    "long" is greater than one year and low
    level refer to characters
    under level 20.


    Characters under level 6
    cannot rent retire.


    Retired Istari cannot get an age
    reset.


    Sauron-listed people cannot retire.


    Characters above level 15 and
    without eq and coins can ask
    any Mw+ to get retired.


    You might be entitled to a full reroll. See help
    reroll for more.





      See also:


      DELETE, REROLL,
      AGE RESET, PRAC RESET,
      RENT, RETROACTIVE
      RETIREMENT

title: RESCUE
body:
(Warrior Skill) [Instant Command]

A rescue is an attempt to make an enemy or enemies hit you instead of the
person being rescued. This is highly usable when playing in groups.

The chance to succeed depends on the how high you know the rescue skill. Typing
rescue with no argument rescues the character that is
buffering. The skill also controls how well you can
protect people.

If cornered, this skill might be one of the more useful to have. By rescuing a
person you put yourself between the person and his enemy, moving him out of
combat and yourself into it. Be aware that a person who is
thrown out of combat like that is rather likely to be
confused for a brief moment.

It takes great agility to master this skill; an iron will and lots of muscle
are important too.

Note: The rescued person will experience some
dizzyness. The better the rescued person knows the
escape skill, the shorter that effect lasts.

Example:

  > rescue morwen





      See also:


      BASH, KICK,
      PROTECT, ESCAPE

title: RESET
body:
[Instant Command]

This command is used to clear your memories of a
bulletin board, marking all messages as unread.

Usage: 'reset'




      See also:


      BOARDS, CATCHUP,
      READ, REPLY,
      WRITE

title: ROPE, TIE
body:
Rope is useful for leading groups in areas that require the
climb skill. The group
leader (i.e., the one who typed group
<someone> ) must have the rope and the others must
follow.

Trying to bring too many people at once may cause someone to fall, so shuttling
is the preferred method. All must be trying to climb, even
if they are not skilled at all.

As an alternative, a rope can be tied from the top of a cliff, to make the
ascent and descent easier:


  > hold rope
  > tie rope [<direction>]

To recover a tied rope, just pick it
up from where it was tied. Of course, you can't expect to
recover a rope from below: you are trusting your
weight to the knot.




      See also:


      CLIMB

title: REVEAL
body:
Syntax:

  reveal <object>
  reveal <character>
  reveal all
  reveal <effort>


  Revealing known hidden objects

reveal <object> allows you to
find an object hidden in a room. You must know what to
look for in order to get it back, but you do not need to have seen the
object before. If you do not know what to look for, use
search.

Unlike search, reveal
<object> succeeds without any skill check.

Example:

  > reveal sword



  Revealing known hidden characters

reveal <character> shows
to your group members the location of a hidden
character you discovered (with
search or because the hidden
character spoke when you could hear him).
Characters not in your group might
realize the presence of the hidden character as well.

Revealing a hostile character allows your
group members to attack him; on the
other hand, if you attack without revealing, you have a
higher chance of taking your enemy by surprise when he is not ready to defend
himself.

reveal all works as reveal
<character>, but it affects any
and all hidden characters that you have discovered.

Examples:

  > reveal scout
  > reveal all


  Searching for and revealing unknown hidden
  characters

reveal <effort>
(quickly, fast, normally,
carefully or thoroughly) is similar to
search
<effort>, but it will reveal any
hidden character you might find to you and your
group. If more than one character
is searching at the same time, reveal is faster than
search, but it decreases the chances of a
surprise attack.

Examples:

  > reveal quickly





      See also:


      HIDE, SEARCH,
      TRACK

title: RETURN
body:
If you have changed shape, use the return command to return to
your original form.




      See also:


      BEARS, METAMORPHS

title: ROLEPLAY, ROLEPLAYING, RP
body:
"Roleplaying" signifies embodying your
character as if they were a genuine inhabitant of
Tolkien's world, complete with a life story,
understandable motivations, and realistic interactions with others and the
environment. It's about more than just accumulating "points" and
"levels."

Our top management strongly supports and encourages roleplay, although it's not
mandatory. Commands that facilitate roleplaying include:



    change description


    Allows you to describe your physical appearance, shaping others'
    perceptions


of you.



    change whois


    Customizes what others see when they type whois
    <your name> — your


reputation and recent exploits may be included.

In various libraries, you'll find
books on roleplaying. While we don't enforce roleplay, we
reserve the right to incentivize it through coded
features. For instance, elves (or
others from the West) who harm peaceful inhabitants may face
alignment consequences, and defenders of good may react
harshly.

Additionally, characters must operate independently
(e.g., no sharing equipment or planning ambushes
together) — see the relevant RULE headings (e.g.,
rules character
separation).

We encourage players who enjoy roleplaying to gather for
shared enjoyment. Feel free to use the idea
command to propose ways in which management can further support your
roleplaying experience.




      See also:


      COMMENT, IN CHARACTER,
      LIBRARY, OUT OF
      CHARACTER

title: RULES
body:
Similar to help, this command displays the
current rules for players of MUME.

rules by itself gives the complete list of headings. rules
<subject> (e.g., rules
account) gives information on
<subject>.

The rules command has the same support for the -v
switch as the help command does. See help
help for more information.

The rules files can also be accessed at
https://mume.org/rules/

title: ROHIRRIM
body:
The Rohirrim are the Horse Lords of Rohan. Their name for
themselves is the Eorlingas. They are tall, blond-haired, and often blue-eyed.
They are by nature stern, fierce, and grave, yet generous. Their native
language is Rohirric. Considered Middle
Men by the Elves and
Dúnedain, they founded few cities (their capital
Edoras is the primary one) but rather have a nomadic culture built around
horses. Their bravery and horsemanship are great assets in
the war against evil.


  MUME Rohirrim

MUME's Rohirrim have a number of bonuses. These include:



    Cheaper rent in Rohan because it is their
    hometown.


    Skilled riders have protection from being thrown off by their
    mounts.


    Their mounts have a decreased chance to refuse to
    move.


    Increased skill when wielding a one-handed or
    two-handed stabbing
    weapons while riding.


    Rohirrim start the game with a bonus in the
    ride skill. This bonus does not make practicing
    ride less effective.





      See also:


      MEN

title: SANCTUARY
fieldBlock:

Accumulative: No

Casting     : Extremely long
Position    : Standing
Level       : Level 18
Class       : Cleric
Min. Mana   : 50
body:
Syntax      : cast 'sanctuary' [recipient]
Type        : Defensive
Accumulative: No
Duration    : Yes
Casting     : Extremely long
Position    : Standing
Level       : Level 18
Class       : Cleric
Min. Mana   : 50

This spell is of only a short and variable duration, but is extremely powerful.
When protected by a sanctuary, the spell will absorb most impact of any form of
attack - may it be magical or physical. However, there are
rumoured to be ways that even sanctuary cannot protect
against, such as falling off a cliff or walking into a particularly nasty trap.

Deep insight and a brilliant mind are quite important when learning this.

Example:


  > cast 'sanctuary'





      See also:


      SHIELD, ARMOUR

title: RSS
body:
MUME's news also get published through a
rss feed. You can subscribe to it on
https://mume.org.

The direct link is
https://mume.org/Import/news/rss
(case sensitve).




      See also:


      NEWS, FORUM, WIKI

title: SADDLE, UNSADDLE
body:
If you want to sit more securely on your
mount, you can buy yourself a saddle and
saddle it. To remove the saddle, use
unsaddle.

Unless you are an Elf, using a saddle will allow you to
ride longer before you become tired.

You can also make your mount drop
items it is carrying using
unsaddle <mount>
<what>, where <what> can be things like
all, money,
all.metal, or sack.

Examples:




> saddle mount



      saddles your mount





> unsaddle mount



      removes the saddle from your mount





> unsaddle mount all



      makes your mount drop everything
      it is carrying





> unsaddle horse all.sword



      makes the horse drop all swords
      it is carrying







      See also:


      RIDE

title: SCOUT
body:
The scout <direction> command allows one to
examine a neighbouring room (in that direction).

Most of the time you will examine that room without going
into it. However, if the exit is some kind of one-way, you
will end up in the other room regardless. If you scout a room that is a
death trap, you will die.

If you are scouting a small room (typically indoor) while not hidden, you will
be spotted by whoever is in it. Otherwise, you have a chance of not being
discovered. Scouting a large room makes it harder to see any hidden content,
but at the same time it is easier to scout it unnoticed, even while not hidden.

The detail level of the scouted room, how you are seen
when discovered, and the scouting delays depend upon the size of the involved
rooms.




      See also:


      "DEATH TRAP"

title: SAVE
body:
Your character is automatically saved every few
minutes or when they die, rent, and
quit.

When you end a session of MUME, your
character will be auto-deleted after a period of time
if you do not log in (this to save disk space, etc). The time it takes for a
character to auto-delete is dependent on
level only. Where it takes only a few days for a
level 1 to get deleted, a level 25
char can be logged off for months (real life) before
deletion. Once a character reaches
level 26 and becomes a legend they will never
delete.

If you type account while on-line, or
list while in the account menu, you will
see how long it will take for your characters to
auto-delete.

Note: The only ways of preventing auto-deletion is to log in on a
regular basis or retire the
character.




      See also:


      RETIRE

title: SECURE ACTIONS
body:
Some idiots think it is fun to abuse unsafe actions to
make people do bad things, here's a thread on how to make your
client actions safe.

For powwow (and on the principle what unsafe-actions do),
here is the explanation from the powwow helpfile:
http://mume.pvv.org/Download/clients/powtty/powwowhelp.txt
(this version here is modified).


  Security

When you define an #action that automatically sends
something back to the MUD you are connected to, you must be
VERY careful since you may allow other players to force
you to execute commands.

Let's explain better: Suppose you define the following
#action:


  #action >+autogroup ^&1 starts following you.={#print;group $1}


Even though this may look harmless, such an action is
potentially lethal, for the following reason:

If you receive a text from the MUD containing something like


  Cauldron ;remove all;drop all;kill dragon starts following you.


It might have been an emote or a
narrate…

powwow will realize that the line matches with the
action you defined (remember that &n can match text
of every length, even if containing spaces or ;) and will execute
this:


  {#print;group Cauldron ;remove all;drop all;kill dragon}


The consequences of such a command can be easily imagined… There are two
strategies to avoid such embarassing situations:



    Use #send and calculator. In fact
    this is NOT dangerous:


#action >+autogroup ^&1 starts following you.= {#print;#send ("group "+$(1))}


    In the worst case you will send some semicolon-separated
    commands to the MUD, but
    MUME does not accept multiple
    commands as clients do.


    Try to use $n instead of &n, so that semicolons and spaces are skipped.

    #action >+autogroup ^$1 starts following
    you.= {#print;group $1}


Note the following is also NOT dangerous:

  #action >+autogroup ^&1 starts following you.=group $1


since if someone tries to force you, as shown above, it will not work, because

action allows only one command to follow the pattern and you did not place
braces around group $1, so only the first command (in this case group
<name>) will be executed.

In any case remember the best strategy is: check what you are doing and if you
are not sure a command is safe, better do not use it.

Last words: You are responsible for your client
and your actions. You will not get reimbursement for
losses due to misconfigured clients, no matter if some
idiot triggered something on purpose or not!




      See also:


      HELP CLIENT, RULES
      ACTIONS

title: SHADOW
body:
Some of the powerful beings wandering Arda nowadays may well leave a shadow
behind after they fall. Such shadows will strive to
protect the corpse they once
occupied.

You can refer to these shadows by adding -shadow to the name of
their previous owner: for example, troll-shadow.




      See also:


      SHADOW OF DEATH

title: SCORE
body:
[Instant Command]

This command will show you basic information about the
health of your character. You
cannot do this while engaged in combat.

You can also out-of-character report your
health, mana, and moves to the room
using score report.

Examples:

  > score
  > score report




      See also:


      STAT, INFO,
      "INFO FORMAT"

title: SCALP
body:
[Delayed Command]

Scalping is a way for members of the evil races to keep
track of whom they have killed.

In order to scalp a corpse, you need to carry an
appropriate tool for the task and type scalp
corpse.

Only higher-level players' corpses can be scalped.




      See also:


      BUTCHER, DRAIN,
      MILK

Type        : Detection
Accumulative: No

Casting     : Normal
Position    : Standing
Level       : Level 7
Class       : Cleric
Min. Mana   : 5

By casting this spell you will be able to sense the presence of hidden or
invisible life forms, although you will have to fathom their identity yourself.
It can only be cast upon oneself, and can
give some protection against sneak
attacks. The spell has a limited duration which increases with your power as a
caster.

Deep insight, a brilliant mind and an iron will are quite important when
learning this.

Example:


  > cast 'sense life'





      See also:


      "DETECT POISON",
      "DETECT EVIL"

title: SEARCH
body:
(Thief skill) [Delayed
Command]

The search skill enables you to search for otherwise hidden
people, exits and objects in the
room.

Searching isn't as easy as it might seem. There are numerous tricks you can
learn about how people and creatures
hide their treasures, or doors, traps or
even themselves! Knowing how to find hidden entrances or
exits is important for any adventurer, I
tell you.

A brilliant mind and good eyesight are quite important when learning this.


  Searching for hidden exits

With a given direction, you search for a secret door in
that way. You need at least one practice session in
search to search for exits. The better you
are, the faster you will find something (if there is anything to discover).

Example:

  > search down
  > open <secret>

Once you have become aware of a hidden exit, you can
interact with it as any normal exit.

If you find a hidden exit, any group
members in the same room will also be made aware of it.


  Searching for hidden objects

search with no arguments finds any object
hidden in the room. The better your skill, the faster the search goes. If you
know what you are looking for, reveal is a
better alternative.

Example:

  > search
  > reveal sword


  Searching for hidden people

Type search <effort> (where
<effort> is one of quickly,
fast, normally, carefully, or
thoroughly) to look for hidden people. Your chances of success
will depend on your eyesight, hearing and sense of smell, as well as on your
search skill.

Example:

  > search q


A succesful search will only make the hidden character
known to you. See reveal to make it known to
your group.


  Searching on bulletin boards

If you are at a bulletin board, you can
search board <text> to find
posts containing <text>.




      See also:


      HIDE, FLUSH,
      SNEAK, REVEAL,
      WATCHTOWERS, BOARDS

If you have a magical anchor or "key" to a location, you might take a
brief look at that place by casting a scry
spell. Your mental intrusion might be noticed by those at that location,
however.

If you cast this spell without any anchor, a mental
map of your outdoor surroundings will form.

To master this spell, a brilliant mind, deep insight and an iron will are
required.

Example:

  > cast 'scry' zoquewhiya





      See also:


      LOCATE, LOCATE LIFE,
      WATCH ROOM

title: SHAKE, SHAKE HANDS, SHAKE HEAD, SHAKE TREE
body:
The shake command is like a normal social
with a minor twist. You can either shake <someone>
or shake head <someone> which will shake your head
at <someone>, or you can shake hands
<someone> which will shake its hands.

If a hungry troll or bear finds that
their prey has climbed into a tree they might be able to shake
tree to force it down.




      See also:


      SOCIALS

title: SEEK
body:
The Last Homely Home of Elrond, also
called Rivendell, is well hidden and any visitor has to
seek the path leading there.

If you are in the correct spot, seek
rivendell may show you the
path to venture - as long as this doesn't endanger the safety of those who live
within the valley.




      See also:


      RIVENDELL

      See also:


      ARMOUR, SANCTUARY

title: SHADOW OF DEATH
body:
When powerful legends die and
return to Arda it can happen they find themselves under a
weakening shadow. Those affected will find their
combat and magical abilites being greatly reduced.

Be warned, while under the shadow you will be very weak
and should not take any risks by walking around in dangerous areas! Thus, it
might be a smart thing to limit yourself to communicating or receiving
equipment your group might have
recovered from your former body.

In general, getting the Shadow of Death is more likely the higher the
level of a character is.

title: SHOOT
body:
shoot is the command used to fire a
missile weapon. If you are
fighting someone already, you can
fire an arrow by typing just
shoot, if you are not already engaged, you can start or join a
fight by typing shoot <victim>.

From time to time, nonmagical missiles will break. This is likely to happen if
you shoot a hard-to-hit target, or when your shot kills
the opponent.




      See also:


      AMMUNITION, ARCHERY,
      RECOVER, MISSILE,
      LOAD, TARGET SHOOTING

Position    : Standing

Class       : Magic User
Min. Mana   : 5

This spell covers the recipient in a shroud of mist, making him quite hard to
be seen. Weak and weak-willed creatures will ignore the
shrouded person completely, and slightly less weak ones will only see him as a
faint shape. Attacking anyone might immediately break the spell, as well as
taking any damage. Hence someone who is bleeding or suffering from the effects
of poison will not be able to remain hidden. If the caster
knows this spell very well, it might resist a few hits.

It takes a brilliant mind to master this spell, and it helps to have deep
insight.

Examples:

  > cast 'shroud'                   cast shroud on yourself
  > hit me                          remove shroud from yourself

title: SHIRE
body:
The Shire is a civilized place located in the old Kingdom of Arthedain. It is
far from the great nations of the South, the nearest other place being
Bree a few miles East. The Shire is divided into four main
parts: the North, South, East and West Farthings. Located east of the Baranduin
(Brandywine) is Buckland. Most Hobbits from the Farthings
consider Bucklanders very queer, while Bucklanders think much the same of the
others. Lying on the Eastern border of Buckland stretches the Old Forest; a
place very few dare to enter.

The Shire was first inhabited in 1601 by a few adventurous
Hobbits from Bree, and since then has
become the main home of Hobbits. There
are no other races living in the Shire, but occasionally
one might see a Dwarf, or two, and sadly many
Elves passing through the South Farthing on their way West,
never to return.


  MUME's Shire

This is the racial home for hobbits.
It is a very peaceful land; sturdy Bounders keep evil orcs
away except under unusual circumstances. The Shire is a collection of several
hobbit villages. To find the shop or
the guild master you are looking for may take a little
walking, but there are very few dangerous beasts to be
found in the Shire (only at the southern and western edges).

If you type map global, the Shire is to be found
westward of the letter B (Bree) at the center of the
map. It extends for about 120 miles, from the east bank of
the Brandywine westward to the village of Michel Delving.




      See also:


      ARDA, BREE, "BLUE
      MOUNTAINS", HOBBITS,
      FORNOST, "GREY
      HAVENS", LÓRIEN,
      RIVENDELL, THARBAD

title: SILVAN
body:
Silvan are wood Elves who live in
Lorien and Mirkwood. They are a secretive people, master
archers, and experts at tracking game within forests. They are considered to be
less wise and more dangerous than other Eldar.


  MUME SILVAN

MUME's Silvan Elves have several
bonuses. These include:



    They have a natural affinity for missile
    weapons and surviving in the wilderness. This
    does not affect practicing the skill.


    They are able to track significantly faster in forests.
    This bonus does not make practicing track less
    effective.


    They are able to parry enemy blows slightly better
    compared to others races when wielding ranged
    weapons.


    They are able to move through forests more easily, as if it were a trail,
    if the land is not gripped by the Shadow.





      See also:


      ELVES

title: SHOPS
body:
Shops are places where the adventurer may purchase
equipment for his quests, and
where he may sell his treasure if he should manage to
survive the perils with his life and sanity intact. Many shops
trade only in a specific type of merchandise. Thus, a baker
may well refuse to buy your armour, even
if it is of high quality!

To some people, the prospect of obtaining the entire
inventory of a shop by murdering the keeper may appear
tempting - but beware: The shopkeepers are very capable of defending
themselves, most would stop you attacking before you'd even really begun.

Examples:


  > list oil
  > buy oil
  > sell pelt




      See also:


      BUY, DYE, SELL,
      LIST, SHOW,
      VALUE, MEND,
      CITIZEN

title: SHUTDOWN
body:
Every once in a long while, MUME will need to be shut down
in order to incorporate new features as well as to
change or update certain game functions.

Shutdowns are used when some manual tinkering with MUME's
data files is necessary before the game is restarted. There is no telling how
long this will take, or how long it will be before the game is up and running
again.

The Aratar can shut the game down at any time and for any
reason, so quit bitching about it.




      See also:


      REBOOT, CRASH

title: SLASHING, SLASHING WEAPONS
body:
(Warrior Skill) (Weapon
Class)

Slashing weapons are generally long blades, with one or two edges. Some of them
are relatively light and easy to handle, and make excellent
parry weapons; some others are longer
and heavier, and are better suited on the offensive side. Of all
weapon types, slashing ones are therefore the most
versatile.

To master this skill, lots of muscle, great agility and good eyesight are
required.

The slashing weapons skill applies to all swordlike
weapons; sabres, swords, scimitars - given that they are
wielded with one hand only.




      See also:


      CHARGE, CLEAVING,
      CONCUSSION, PIERCING,
      STABBING, TWO-HANDED

Min. Mana   : 15

Accumulative: No
